sources.citation: Mühlhäusler, Peter. 2013. Norf'k. In Michaelis, Maurer, Haspelmath & Huber (eds.), APiCS Online, survey chapter 24.https://apics-online.info/surveys/24
sources.note: §4 Phonology covers vowel phonemes, consonants, clusters and diphthongs; no mention of word stress or accent (only 'rising intonation' of yes-no questions in §8).
Vowel chart cited to Harrison 1972 p. 18; no statement on stress; Pitkern article reproduces Gimson's IPA transcription from Ross & Moverley 1964 pp. 121-135 without prosodic commentary.

sources.citation: Nash, Joshua. 2011. Insular toponymies: pristine place-naming on Norfolk Island, South Pacific and Dudley Peninsula, Kangaroo Island, South Australia. PhD thesis, University of Adelaide (digital.library.adelaide.edu.au item f6482abb-ffc0-4302-b9c2-a781e7b5c8c3).
sources.note: No phonology section; one toponym entry (no. 284 'Down ar Graveyard') notes 'Pronunciation: stress on second syllable of "graveyard" in Norf'k' — a single-word datum, not a rule.

sources.citation: Källgård, Anders. 1998. A Pitkern word list. In P. Mühlhäusler (ed.), Papers in Pidgin and Creole Linguistics No. 5, 107-171. Pacific Linguistics A-91. DOI 10.15144/PL-A91.107 (ANU Open Research / sealang).
sources.note: Word list only; each active entry has a phonetic transcription with a primary-stress mark (e.g. APE [a'pe], BARGAIN ['bo:gen], APAHAMA ['apa'hama]) but no statement of a stress rule.

sources.citation: Flint, E. H. 1961. Bilingual interaction between Norfolk Island language and English. Paper, First Conference of the Linguistic Circle of Canberra, 20 May 1961 (ANU Open Research item 1f30c7a9-4a88-4de1-86d9-cd49f6971ed8).
sources.note: Intelligibility study; 'prosodic features' appear only as a category of listener failures (2.88% / 1.3%); nothing on stress placement.
